purpose: Measured construction evidence for authored masonry, timber, and door-hardware assets. A value in this file is evidence, not permission to blend unrelated periods or scale different members independently.

evidence_classes.surveyed: Direct dimensions published from a building or archaeological survey.
evidence_classes.catalogued: Direct dimensions published by the museum or collection holding the object.
evidence_classes.laboratory_characterized: Composition or physical properties measured from material samples using published laboratory methods.
evidence_classes.project_measured: Dimension read from the evaluated iggy3d asset, not from the historical source.
evidence_classes.derived: Calculated from published or project-measured dimensions; the calculation is stated.
evidence_classes.technical_guidance: A numeric working value published by an authoritative technical guide; it is not a measurement of the selected historic building.
evidence_classes.qualitative: Source-backed construction information without a numeric dimension.
evidence_classes.unsupported: A number currently present in an iggy3d recipe for which no measurement authority has been identified.

stone.use_limit: A coherent Cordoba early-Gothic ashlar family. Do not describe these dimensions as universal English or French cathedral dimensions.

stone.period: 13th-14th century church fabric; Tortonian source stone
stone.location: Santa Marina de Aguas Santas and the likely Naranjo quarry, Cordoba, Spain
stone.lithology: Yellowish clastic sandy biocalcarenite and fine sandy biomicrite with carbonated micritic cement.
stone.grain_size: Medium, with abundant fragmented microfauna; the paper does not publish a sieve-derived numeric grain distribution.
stone.color_cause: Visible iron oxyhydroxides produce the more saturated yellow Naranjo color.
rare_lithotypes: conglomeratic biocalcarenite with greater-than-2-mm non-carbonate clasts
stone.surface_relief_depth_status: unknown; the scaled figures establish lateral identity and frequency but not relief depth
stone.optical_roughness_status: unknown; the paper does not publish a PBR roughness or gloss measurement
stone.use_limit: The intact core uses the dominant Santa Marina/Naranjo biocalcarenite body. Rare conglomeratic and biosparite faces require explicit variants and may not be scattered universally. Porosity and fossil percentages describe the rock body; they are not permission to paint the same fraction of the surface as black holes.

stone.period: fresh quarry reference sample measured for a 2019 conservation study
stone.lithology: Yellowish coarse-grained calcarenite used as building stone.
stone.height_distribution_interpretation: Negative skew represents a surface dominated by the upper body with sparse deeper valleys. The published 3D map shows angular and elongated grains rather than circular cellular noise.
stone.use_limit: This is a relief proxy from a comparable yellow coarse calcarenite, not the Santa Marina or Naranjo stone and not a medieval dressed-face scan. It may constrain stone-body relief scale and distribution only. It does not authorize tool-mark depth, block-plane deformation, arris rounding, mortar recession, damage, weathering, or PBR roughness values.

stone.observed_relation: The paper notes larger mean ashlar length closer to the source quarry.
stone.use_limit: Population statistics are valuable variation evidence but are not a course recipe. Preserve building and phase identity rather than drawing independent Gaussian widths and heights.

stone.joint_width: A few millimetres; the source does not publish one universal numeric width.
stone.profile: Narrow and commonly flush for high-quality ashlar.
stone.use_limit: Select an exact width from a building-specific measured reference. Eleven- to fourteen-millimetre joints cannot be labelled fine ashlar joints.

stone.profile: The 3 mm value is used for narrow ashlar-joint mortar grading.
stone.use_limit: This is a published numeric working value, not a measured joint from the selected Cordoba churches. Retain that limitation in the asset manifest.

stone.direction: Characteristically diagonal on the recorded medieval fragments; some visible faces carried closely set vertical claw marks.
stone.use_limit: Spacing is measured evidence for this excavated Caen-stone assemblage, not a universal stroke prescription.

stone.location: former diocese of Toul, southern Lorraine
stone.organization: Finishing marks are often oblique; individual faces may be parallel, slightly fanned, chevroned, crossed, or disordered. The mason works inward from an arris to avoid spalling.
stone.selected_family: Fine oblique parallel layage with slight fan variation; crossed, chevroned, toothed, point, and unfinished coarse faces remain separate finish families.
stone.depth_status: No groove depth is published for the surveyed fine layage.
stone.use_limit: This is an 11th-12th-century southern-Lorraine comparative finish study, not a Cordoba face survey. It may constrain finite mark length, width, density, overlap logic, and working organization, but it does not authorize groove depth or identify one exact mason.
Ooids are material-body grains. They do not justify centimetre-scale cellular noise.
Portland limestone evidence only. Use when the authored stone family is explicitly oolitic limestone.
These are repair and break dimensions, not permission to distribute damage across every block.
The catalogue envelope does not reveal the moulding profile, projection, or repeat. A measured profile drawing or direct 3D survey is still required.
The catalogue envelope does not establish dogtooth motif width, height, depth, or centre spacing.

brick.use_limit: A Great Brick family, not a generic modern brick.

brick.observed_form: Irregular shape, slightly rounded arrises, pebble and angular flint inclusions.
Irregular arrises, rough faces, large pebble inclusions, shallow horizontal drying creases.

wood.joinery: Rebated boards; housed oak ledges let in flush; original centre ledge blind-pegged.
wood.surface_evidence: Cross-grain finishing, surviving saw marks, router marks in the ledge housing, and coarse-stone abrasion.

wood.joinery: Three vertical oak planks assembled closely to one another and to the opening.

wood.period: floor associated with a beam felled 1465-1497
wood.observed_form: Lower joist edges chamfered; some chamfers terminate in plain notched stops; some boards use wooden tongues in opposing grooves.
Earlier boards were more worn; reused boards retained doubled nail holes.

wood.use_limit: The catalogue depth includes the assembled wood and iron object. It is not evidence that every plank is 165 mm thick.

The source establishes square true arrises and 1-4 mm tool spacing but not arris radius or groove depth, so neither is authored.

findings: No measured profile drawing supports the four current moulding cross-sections.

findings: The face scale overlaps some later hand-made brick populations but does not match either surveyed family in this ledger.
If S14 Ightfield infill brick is selected, seven 230-235 mm bricks plus 10 mm perpends require a row pitch near 1.68-1.715 m, not the current 1.6 m.
The recipe has no brick depth, header face, frog state, or geometry placement contract.

The running bond is a valid explicit choice only after it is tied to a named wall or design brief.

findings: The project door is not a uniform enlargement of the Met, Westminster, or Tallinn door.
The three principal project boards are 680-739 mm wide, 128-131 mm thick, and 4.76-4.80 m long.
Its dimensions are valid project facts, but each giant-scale adaptation ratio still needs an explicit design authority.
The Met object is a valid colour and assembly reference; its 165 mm overall catalogue depth is not a valid plank-thickness measurement.
structural_oak_door_v1.status: project geometry measured; historical-to-giant adaptation remains undocumented

unresolved_measurements.required: The Córdoba family now bounds the intact facing wythe. Obtain a stone-for-stone elevation and building-specific joint survey before claiming reconstruction of one named church rather than a bounded family translation.
Obtain scaled cross-sections or a licensed 3D survey for every roll, cavetto, cyma, fillet, dogtooth, and leaf band.
Measure intact arris radius, tooling depth, isolated chip envelopes, and fracture planes from scaled close-ups or scan data.
Record exact joint width and profile per chosen wall phase; do not use one universal mortar recess.
Measure one named corner bond, quoin sequence, total wall thickness, backing wythe, fill, and through-stone placement before generating returns or a structural wall core.
Measure jamb bond, opening span, intrados and extrados radii, voussoir wedges, ring depth, springing, skewbacks, and through-depth joints before restoring the former generic arch fixture.
Define one approved player-to-giant scale transform and state which members scale structurally rather than uniformly.
Document plank edge joints, ledge and brace housings, peg diameters, hinge thickness, pintles, nail heads, and clearances for the chosen door family.
Portfolio renders establish visual quality, not dimensions. Exact BG3 asset dimensions remain unverified unless measured through Larian's officially supplied Toolkit assets under its terms.
